questions.question: Article 40 of the Indian constitution, "Organisation of village panchayats", is a _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:-**

 
 
• Articles 36-51 of Part-IV of the Indian Constitution deals with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). 
 
• They are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. 
 
• DPSPs are non-justiciable i.e non-enforceable in the court of law.
 
• They act as directives to the government to create any law.
 
• They act as the ‘instrument of instructions’.
 
• **Article 40 is with respect to the Organisation of village panchayats. (Hence option 1 is correct).**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental duties:-

 
 
• ​These are a set of moral obligations that are mentioned in the Constitution of India.
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.
 
• These duties are not enforceable by law but are expected to be followed by every citizen as a means of promoting a spirit of patriotism and upholding the ideals of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• Fundamental Rights:-
 
 
• FRs are known as the base of the Indian constitution & mentioned in Part III of the constitution.
 
• They prohibit unreasonable interference of the state & prevent its executive & legislature to become authoritarian, hence putting due limitations on state power.
 
 
 
• Legal right:-
 
 
• It is an interest accepted and protected by law.
 
• It is a claim that a person has against another person or against the state. Legal rights can be enforced through the courts.

questions.question: The day to day condition of the atmosphere at a place with respect to the temperature humidity, rainfall. wind speed etc. is called _______ at the place.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weather**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Weather:-**

 
 
• It is the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time with respect to heat, cloudiness, dryness, sunshine, wind, and rain.
 
• **It is a short-term phenomenon that can vary from day to day, hour to hour, or even minute to minute. (Hence option 2 is correct).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate:-**

 
 
• This on the other hand, is the average weather conditions in a particular place over a long period of time, typically at least 30 years.
 
• Climate is influenced by a number of factors, including latitude, altitude, distance from the ocean, and prevailing winds.
 
 
 
• **Environment:-**
 
 
• It is the surroundings in which we live and work.
 
• It includes the air, water, land, and all living things.
 
• The environment is important because it provides us with the resources we need to survive and thrive.
 
 
 
• **Ecology:-**
 
 
• It is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment.
 
• It considers organisms at the individual, population, community, ecosystem, and biosphere level.

questions.question: The disease-causing microbes are called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Pathogens**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Pathogens:-**

__
 
• **The disease-causing microbes are called pathogens. **
 
• Pathogens can be viruses, bacteria, fungi, protozoa, or helminths (worms).
 
• They can cause a wide range of diseases, from mild to severe, and can be transmitted in a variety of ways, including through direct contact, contaminated food or water, or insect bites. 
 
• Examples of common diseases caused by different types of pathogens:
 
 
• **Viruses**: COVID-19, influenza, measles, mumps, rubella, HIV/AIDS, herpes, rabies
 
• **Bacteria**: Strep throat, pneumonia, tuberculosis, cholera, salmonellosis, Lyme disease
 
• **Fungi**: Athlete's foot, ringworm, candidiasis, histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis
 
• **Protozoa**: Malaria, toxoplasmosis, giardia, amoebiasis
 
• **Helminths**: Ascariasis, hookworm, tapeworm, trichinosis
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposers:-**

 
 
• These are organisms that break down dead or decaying organisms and organic matter.
 
• They play a vital role in ecosystems by recycling nutrients and making them available to other organisms.
 
• Decomposers can be found in all environments, from soil and water to forests and deserts.
 
 
 
• **Toxin:-**
 
 
• It is a poisonous substance produced within living cells or organisms.
 
 
 
• **Antibodies:-**
 
 
• It is also known as immunoglobulins, are proteins produced by the immune system in response to infection.
 
• They are an important part of the body's defense system as they work to destroy disease-causing organisms (such as viruses or bacteria) and block them from infecting human cells.

questions.question: The substances which reduce friction are called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lubricants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lubricants:-**

 
 
• **These are substances that are introduced between two surfaces in contact in order to reduce friction. (Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• They do this by forming a thin layer between the surfaces, which prevents them from rubbing directly against each other.
 
• This reduces the amount of heat generated and the wear and tear on the surfaces. 
 
• There are many different types of lubricants, including:
 
 
• Oils
 
• Greases
 
• Solids, such as graphite and molybdenum disulfide
 
• Liquids, such as water and silicone
 
• Gases, such as air and nitrogen
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluids:-**

 
 
• **These are substances that can flow easily and continuously deform under an applied shear stress, or external force. **
 
• They have zero shear modulus, or, in simpler terms, are substances which cannot resist any shear force applied to them.
 
 
 
• **Magnet:-**
 
 
• **It is a material or object that produces a magnetic field. **
 
• This magnetic field is invisible but is responsible for the most notable property of a magnet: a force that pulls on other ferromagnetic materials, such as iron, steel, nickel, cobalt, etc. and attracts or repels other magnets.
 
 
 
• **Spring:-**
 
 
• **It is an elastic object that stores mechanical energy and releases it when the opposing force is removed. **
 
• Springs can be made from a variety of materials, including metal, plastic, and rubber.
 
• They come in all shapes and sizes, and can be used in a wide variety of applications.

questions.question: In 1927, B.R Ambedkar started which movement with Dalits?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temple entry movement.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Temple entry movement:-**

 
 
• **The Temple Entry Movement was a social movement in India that campaigned for the right of all Hindus, regardless of caste, to enter Hindu temples.**
 
• It was a major part of the Indian independence movement and played a crucial role in the fight against caste discrimination.
 
• **In 1927, B.R Ambedkar started this movement with Dalits.**
 
• The movement began in the early 20th century, when a number of social reformers began to challenge the practice of untouchability. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Respect Movement:-**

 
 
• **It was a social movement in South India that began in the early 20th century. **
 
• It was founded by E.V. Ramasamy
 
• It aimed to achieve a society in which oppressed castes have equal human rights, and encouraging backward castes to have self-respect in the context of a caste-based society that considered them to be a lower end of the hierarchy.
 
 
 
• **Equal Pay Movement:-**
 
 
• **It is a social movement that campaigns for equal pay for equal work, regardless of gender. **
 
• The movement has a long history, dating back to the early 19th century, but it gained momentum in the mid-20th century with the rise of the women's rights movement.
 
 
 
• **Indian independence movement:-**
 
 
• **It was a series of historic events with the ultimate aim of ending British rule in India.**
 
• It lasted from the mid-19th century to 1947, when India gained independence.

questions.question: "Solung" is a festival celebrated by the Adi Tribe of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Solung:-

 
 
• Solung is the most popular festival of the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, India. (Hence option 4 is correct)
 
• It is a post-harvest festival celebrated at the beginning of September every year to give thanks to the gods for a bountiful harvest and to pray for good fortune in the coming year.
 
• The main highlight of the Solung festival is the Ponung dance, a traditional Adi dance performed by women of all ages.
 
 
 
• **Adi Tribe:-**
 
 
• The Adi tribe is one of the largest indigenous peoples in the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh, with a population of over 1.1 million.
 
• They are also found in small numbers in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
 
• The Adi tribe is composed of 14 sub-tribes, each with its own unique dialect and customs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Kullu Dussehra, Losar Festival, Halda Festival, Sazo Festival, Doongri Fair, Phulaich Festival, Kasol Music Festival
 
 

 **Andhra Pradesh **
 Pongal, Ugadi, Vinayaka Chaturthi, Visakha Utsav, Tirupati Tirumala, Brahmotsavam, Lumbini Festival, Rayalaseema Food & Dance Festival

questions.question: Which river flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narmada**:-

 
 
• **The Narmada River flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges in central India. (Hence option 1 is correct).**
 
• It is one of the oldest rivers in the world, and is considered to be sacred by Hindus.
 
• The Narmada River flows west for 1,312 kilometers before draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Godavari River:-**

 
 
• It originates from Nasik and rises at an elevation of 1,067 m from Trimbakeshwar (Nasik district of Maharashtra), 80 km from the Arabian Sea.
 
• Godavari's total length from its origin to its outfall into the Bay of Bengal is 1,465 km. 
 
 
 
• **Son River:-**
 
 
• It originates from the Amarkantak plateau in the Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh. 
 
• It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, and Jharkhand and finally joins Ganga in Bihar near Patna.
 
• The Bansagar Dam in Madhya Pradesh is also on the Son river.
 
 
 
• **Mahanadi River**
 
 
• It is a river in central India, rising in the hills of southeastern Chhattisgarh state and has a total course of 858 kilometers (533 mi). 
 
• The river originates from Sihawa Mountain in Chhattisgarh.
 
• The largest dam, the Hirakud Dam is built on the river.

questions.question: Which famous Indian musician is associated with musical instrument Santoor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma:-**

 
 
• **He was an Indian classical musician and santoor player. (Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
• He is credited with adapting the santoor for Indian classical music and popularizing it around the world. 
 
• Sharma was awarded many prestigious awards for his contributions to music, including the Padma Shri (1991), the Padma Vibhushan (2001), and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1986). He was also conferred an honorary doctorate by the University of Jammu.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Hariprasad Chaurasia:-**

 
 
• **He is an Indian bansuri (bamboo flute) player, known for his contributions to Hindustani classical music. **
 
• He is popularly known as the "Magician of the Flute" and is considered a great revolutionary in the field of flute playing.
 
 
 
• **Ustad Zakir Hussain:-**
 
 
• **He is a renowned Indian tabla player, composer, percussionist, music producer, and film actor. **
 
• He is the son of tabla player Alla Rakha, and is widely considered to be one of the greatest tabla players of all time.
 
 
 
• **Ustad Amjad Ali Khan:-**
 
 
• **He is the sixth generation sarod player in his family, and his ancestors have developed and shaped the instrument over two hundred years. **
 
• He learned from his father Haafiz Ali Khan, who was a court musician in Gwalior up until Independence in 1947.

questions.question: Under the Delhi Sultanate, a religious tax ________ was imposed on the wealthy and rich Muslims in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zakat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zakat:-**

 
 
• It is one of the five pillars of Islam and is a compulsory tax on all Muslims who meet certain wealth criteria.
 
• **Under the Delhi Sultanate, it was imposed on the wealthy and rich Muslims in India. (Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
• The proceeds from zakat are used to help the poor and needy, as well as to support other Islamic causes. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Other taxes of Delhi Sultanate are:-**

 
• **Kharaj: **

 
 
• This was a land tax levied on all agricultural land, regardless of the religion of the owner.
 
• The rate of kharaj varied, but it was typically around 50% of the produce.
 
 
 
• **Jizya: **
 
 
• This was a poll tax levied on all non-Muslim adult males.
 
• The jizya was a religious tax, but it was also a way for the Sultans to assert their dominance over the non-Muslim population.
 
 
 
• **Khams: **
 
 
• This was a tax on the spoils of war.
 
• One-fifth of all war booty was given to the Sultan, while the rest was divided among the soldiers who had participated in the campaign.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter is known as the mother of the Indian revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madan Bhikaji Cama**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madam Bhikaji Cama:-**

 
 
• **She is known as the mother of the Indian revolution. **
 
• She was the first person to unfurl the Indian flag on foreign soil, at the International Socialist Conference in Stuttgart, Germany, on August 22, 1907.
 
• The flag she unfurled was a tricolour of green, saffron, and red, with the words "Bande Mataram" (Hail to the Mother) written on it.
 
• **She was a strong advocate for women's education and rights. She was also a vocal critic of British colonial rule in India.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarojini Naidu:-**

 
 
• **She was a prominent Indian independence fighter, politician, poet, and social activist. **
 
• **She is known as the "Nightingale of India".**
 
• Sarojini Naidu was also a poet, and she wrote many poems and plays. Her poems were generally inspired by Indian culture and traditions. Sarojini Naidu received many awards for her poems, including the "Sahitya Akademi Award" and the "Padma Vibhushan".
 
 
 
• **Annie Besant:-**
 
 
• **She was a British socialist, theosophist, freemason, women's rights and Home Rule activist, educationist, and campaigner for Indian nationalism. **
 
• She was an ardent supporter of both Irish and Indian self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Aruna Asaf Ali:-**
 
 
• She was an Indian educator, political activist, and publisher.
 
• **An active participant in the Indian independence movement, she is widely remembered for hoisting the Indian National flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan, Bombay during the Quit India Movement in 1942.**

questions.question: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) is regulated by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India:-**

 
 
• RBI is India's central bank and regulatory body responsible for regulation of the Indian banking system.
 
• It is under the ownership of Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
 
• **It is responsible for the control, issue and maintaining supply of the Indian rupee. **
 
• **The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). (Hence option 3 is correct).**
 
 
 
• **Small Industries Development Bank of India:-**
 
 
• SIDBI is a financial institution that was established in 1990 to promote, finance, and develop the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) sector in India.
 
• SIDBI is the apex regulatory body for overall licensing and regulation of micro, small and medium enterprise finance companies in India. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** State Bank of India:-**

 
 
• **SBI is the largest commercial bank in India by assets and the largest public sector bank in India by deposits. **
 
• It is a government-owned corporation headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• In 1955, the Imperial Bank of India was nationalized and renamed the State Bank of India
 
 
 
• **Indian Bank:-**
 
 
• **It is a public sector bank in India, founded in 1907. **
 
• It is headquartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu and has over 5,800 branches and 4,900 ATMs across India.
 
 
 
• **ICICI Bank Limited:-**
 
 
• **It is an Indian multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra. **
 
• It was founded in 1994 by the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI), a government-owned financial institution.

questions.question: Provisions related to the Municipalities are mentioned under which part of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IX A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Part IX-A of the Indian constitution deals with municipalities.

 
 
• It was added by the 74th amendment act of the Indian constitution.
 
• The 74th amendment act was introduced in 1992.
 
• It came into force on 1st June 1993.
 
• Part IX-A of the Indian constitution covers Article 243 P to 243 ZG.
 
• The act added a new twelfth schedule to the Indian constitution.
 
• The first municipal corporation in India was set up in Madras in 1688.
 
• The Municipal Corporation of Bombay and Calcutta was set up in 1726.

questions.question: Which among the following plant kingdoms are divided into dicotyledons and monocotyledons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Angiosperms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Angiosperms**:-

 
 
• These are the flowering plants, and they are the largest and most diverse group of plants on Earth. 
 
• They are found in all habitats, from deserts to rainforests, and they include a wide variety of plants, such as trees, shrubs, herbs, and grasses. 
 
• **The Angiosperms are divided into dicotyledons and monocotyledons.**
 
 
 
• **Dicotyledons:-**
 
 
• These are angiosperms that have two seed leaves, or cotyledons.
 
 
 
• **Monocotyledons:-**
 
 
• These are angiosperms that have one seed leaf.
 
• These two groups of plants differ in many other ways, including their vascular system, root structure, leaf structure, and flower structure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gymnosperms:-**

 
 
• **These are seed-producing plants that produce "naked seeds," meaning that the seeds are not enclosed in an ovary or fruit.**
 
• Gymnosperms are the oldest group of seed plants, and they have been around for over 300 million years.
 
 
 
• **Bryophytes:-**
 
 
• **These are a group of non-vascular land plants that includes mosses, liverworts, and hornworts. **
 
• Bryophytes are found in all parts of the world, except for the driest deserts.
 
• They are most common in moist, shady environments, but they can also be found in extreme habitats, such as the Arctic and Antarctica.
 
 
 
• **Pteridophytes:-**
 
 
• **These are vascular plants that reproduce by spores. **
 
• They are also known as cryptogams, meaning that their reproductive structures are hidden.

questions.question: Which among the following type of unemployment is also known as the real wage unemployment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**classical**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Real wage unemployment:-**

 
• **It is a type of classical unemployment. (Hence option 1 is correct)**
 
• It occurs when the real wage is set above the equilibrium real wage.
 
• **The equilibrium real wage is the wage that is consistent with full employment, meaning that everyone who wants to work at the prevailing wage rate can find a job.**
 
• Real wage unemployment can be caused by a number of factors, including:
 
 
• **Minimum wage laws:** Minimum wage laws set a legal minimum wage that employers must pay their workers. If the minimum wage is set above the equilibrium real wage, it can lead to real wage unemployment.
 
• **Collective bargaining agreements:** Collective bargaining agreements are contracts between unions and employers that set wages and other working conditions. If a union negotiates a wage rate that is above the equilibrium real wage, it can lead to real wage unemployment.
 
• **Efficiency wages:** Some firms may choose to pay their workers wages above the equilibrium real wage in order to boost worker productivity and morale. However, if all firms do this, it can lead to real wage unemployment.

questions.question: Nalanda University, an important centre in ancient period is situated in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nalanda University:-**

 
 
• It is considered as the world's first residential university and among the greatest centers of learning in the ancient world.
 
• **It was located near the city of Rajagriha (now Rajgir) and about 90 kilometres (56 mi) southeast of Pataliputra (now Patna).**
 
• Nalanda was founded in the 5th century CE and flourished for over 700 years, attracting scholars and students from all over Asia.
 
• It was a major center for the study of Buddhism, as well as other subjects such as philosophy, logic, mathematics, astronomy, and medicine.
 
• **The university was destroyed by the invading armies of Bakhtiyar Khilji in 1200 CE, but it remains an important symbol of India's rich cultural heritage.**
 
• In 2010, a new Nalanda University was established in Rajgir, near the site of the ancient university. The new university is an international and research-intensive university that offers postgraduate programs in a variety of disciplines. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihar:-**

 
 
• It is a state in eastern India.
 
• It is the third largest state by population, the 12th largest by area, and the 14th largest by GDP in 2021.
 
• Bihar borders Uttar Pradesh to its west, Nepal to the north, the northern part of West Bengal to the east, and Jharkhand to the south.

questions.question: Which former Miss India, also the recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, popularised Indian classical dance in the west?

• Indrani trained in a variety of classical dance forms, including Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, and Odissi.
 
• **She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and popularised Indian classical dance in the west. (Hence option 3 is correct).**
